question: How does original observed animal travel in relation to solar azimuth and ERA5 shortwave vary along biogeographical climate gradients, and which macro gradients persist within an original taxon/study?
outcome: Previously computed within-tagged animal, calendar month x four-hour apparent-solar-time mean effect of +100 W/m2 ERA5 shortwave on cos(GPS travel bearing minus Sun azimuth). Do not re-estimate it.
exploratory_macro_axes: mean cosine(wind-flow-to direction minus Sun azimuth)
absolute latitude proxy from source 15-degree band midpoint

analysis.source_environment_averaging: Equal native taxon x selected 1degree grid x original calendar year context means; one equal unit per source study.
analysis.between_studies: Spearman source-level rho and source leave-one-out min/max, overall 20 and first/external 10 each, plus 5000 source resampling descriptive percentile intervals.
analysis.within_studies: Only same native taxon with two original preselected contexts, compute slope(high covariate)-slope(low covariate), average if multiple same-taxon pairs within one source, then aggregate source units.
analysis.missing_effects: All 28 without shortwave effect are retained with UNAVAILABLE; never zero-impute.

limits: Gridded ERA5 shortwave is not actual body solar exposure or microhabitat shading.
Sun altitude, route geometry, season and fine solar clock may confound remaining 4-hour matched effects.
Study/clade/geography/telemetry source selection nonrandom and severely imbalanced.
Wind at 100m is not validated flight-altitude wind.
Within-study source comparisons may reuse individuals and do not represent independent field populations.
No animal track coordinates, IDs or precise UTC fix timestamps should be redistributed.
next_route: Separate prospective source-frozen physical test: residualize ERA5 shortwave on true solar altitude, local fine solar clock and season within animal/study, model both cos and sin sun-relative travel with wind, and reserve untouched independent source archives.
